'''Dichotomous thinking''' or '''binary thinking''' in [[statistics]] is the process of seeing a discontinuity in the possible values that a [[p-value]] can take during [[Statistical hypothesis testing|null hypothesis significance testing]]: it is either above the significance threshold (usually 0.05) or below. When applying dichotomous thinking, a first p-value of 0.0499 will be interpreted the same as a p-value of 0.0001 (the null hypothesis is rejected) while a second p-value of 0.0501 will be interpreted the same as a p-value of 0.7 (the null hypothesis is accepted). The fact that first and second p-values are mathematically very close is thus completely disregarded and values of p are not considered as continuous but are interpreted dichotomously with respect to the significance threshold. A common measure of dichotomous thinking is the [[cliff effect]].<ref name="lai">{{cite web |url=https://iase-web.org/documents/papers/icots8/ICOTS8_C101_LAI.pdf |title=DICHOTOMOUS THINKING: A PROBLEM BEYOND NHST |last= Lai |first= Jerry |date= 2019 |website= |publisher=ICOTS8 |access-date=23 October 2018 |quote=}}</ref> A reason to avoid dichotomous thinking is that p-values and other statistics naturally change from study to study due to random variation alone;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cumming |first=Geoff |date=2014 |title=The New Statistics: Why and How |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0956797613504966 |journal=Psychological Science |language=en |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=7–29 |doi=10.1177/0956797613504966 |pmid=24220629 |s2cid=3484092 |issn=0956-7976|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berner |first1=Daniel |last2=Amrhein |first2=Valentin |date=2022 |title=Why and how we should join the shift from significance testing to estimation |journal=Journal of Evolutionary Biology |volume=35 |issue=6 |language=en |pages=777–787 |doi=10.1111/jeb.14009 |pmid=35582935 |pmc=9322409 |issn=1010-061X}}</ref> decisions about refutation or support of a scientific hypothesis based on a result from a single study are therefore not reliable.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Amrhein |first1=Valentin |last2=Greenland |first2=Sander |last3=McShane |first3=Blake |date=2019 |title=Scientists rise up against statistical significance |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=567 |issue=7748 |pages=305–307 |doi=10.1038/d41586-019-00857-9|pmid=30894741 |s2cid=84186074 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Dichotomous thinking is very often associated with p-value reading<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rosenthal | first1=Robert | last2=Gaito | first2=John | title=The Interpretation of Levels of Significance by Psychological Researchers | journal=The Journal of Psychology | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=55 | issue=1 | year=1963 | issn=0022-3980 | doi=10.1080/00223980.1963.9916596 | pages=33–38 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Nelson | first1=Nanette | last2=Rosenthal | first2=Robert | last3=Rosnow | first3=Ralph L. | title=Interpretation of significance levels and effect sizes by psychological researchers. | journal=American Psychologist | publisher=American Psychological Association (APA) | volume=41 | issue=11 | year=1986 | issn=1935-990X | doi=10.1037/0003-066x.41.11.1299 | pages=1299–1301 }}</ref><ref>{{cite conference | last1=Besançon | first1=Lonni | last2=Dragicevic | first2=Pierre | title=Extended Abstracts of the 2019 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems | chapter=The Continued Prevalence of Dichotomous Inferences at CHI | publisher=ACM Press | location=New York, New York, USA | year=2019 | pages=1–11 | isbn=978-1-4503-5971-9 | doi=10.1145/3290607.3310432 }}</ref> but it can also happen with other statistical tools such as interval estimates.<ref name="lai"/><ref name="Helske Helske Cooper Ynnerman pp. 3397–3409">{{cite journal | last1=Helske | first1=Jouni | last2=Helske | first2=Satu | last3=Cooper | first3=Matthew | last4=Ynnerman | first4=Anders | last5=Besancon | first5=Lonni | title=Can Visualization Alleviate Dichotomous Thinking? Effects of Visual Representations on the Cliff Effect | journal=IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=27 | issue=8 | date=2021 | issn=1077-2626 | doi=10.1109/tvcg.2021.3073466| arxiv=2002.07671 | pages=3397–3409| pmid=33856998 | s2cid=233230810 }}</ref>
